blocks.text: The client API mirrors the ownership model. Proposal generation returns content, a separate read composes current evidence and eligibility, and approve accepts only an ApprovalCommand. Acceptance means the command was recorded, not that every record changed. Cancel and rollback have their own identities because they express different intent and can produce different authoritative outcomes.

blocks.title: UI-facing contract behavior
rows: Malformed content becomes a bounded error with Retry; no product action is available
Evidence and eligibility were checked at checkedAt
Stale or restricted rows remain readable and name what must be refreshed
The idempotent command was accepted for processing
Keep rows pending and poll or subscribe until ActionOutcome resolves
The service recorded or rejected cancellation intent
Continue reconciliation because a late result can supersede the request
A compensating command was accepted for eligible successes
Render its per-item outcome separately from the original bulk edit

blocks.text: Create one commandId for one approval click and reuse it after a lost response. The service returns the earlier receipt or outcome for the same payload and rejects a different payload under that identity. A new approval after changing selected records gets a new ID. Cancel uses cancelCommandId, and rollback uses rollbackCommandId plus tokens issued only for confirmed reversible successes. AbortSignal stops the browser from waiting; it never changes the product status by itself.
